The Opportunity


RoaDo helps shippers and logistics teams run domestic and cross-border freight on one connected platform. As a Product Manager, you'll take charge of one area of that platform. Depending on business needs at the time you join, it could be load planning, carrier sourcing and spot bidding, shipment visibility, our AI-driven control tower, digital proof of delivery, freight billing, or our export-import (EXIM) workflows. You'll partner with engineers, operations teams, and enterprise clients to turn real logistics problems into products that deliver clear business results.


Your Responsibilities

• Set the product direction and quarterly priorities for your area, and see them through to delivery

• Take full ownership of how users get work done in your module, from first sketch to everyday adoption

• Strengthen how RoaDo connects with the outside world: client ERPs, transporter systems, GPS and telematics devices, shipping lines, forwarders, customs brokers, and port terminals

• Give customers a single view of their international shipments, from factory gate to port, across the sea or air leg, and on to final delivery

• Spend regular time with exporters, importers, transporters, forwarders, and finance teams to find where work breaks down and decide what to fix first

• Write detailed requirement documents that leave little room for interpretation, and stay close to the engineering team through each sprint

• Choose the right success measures, such as usage, turnaround time, port dwell, and cost per shipment, and report on them consistently


What We're Looking For

• 5 to 7 years in product management, including at least 2 years running a B2B software product with full accountability

• Solid knowledge of road freight in India, both full-truckload and part-load, including how loads are planned, how transporters are selected, how trips are tracked, and how freight bills are settled

• Practical understanding of the truckload lifecycle: placing orders with transporters, monitoring trip milestones, handling waiting charges, and closing payments

• Good knowledge of export-import operations, including space booking, container handling at CFS and ICD, port movement, customs filing, and coordination with shipping lines and forwarders

• Comfort with core trade documents and terms such as Bill of Lading, Shipping Bill, Bill of Entry, Incoterms, and demurrage and detention charges

• Experience with exception alerts, live visibility, or control-tower style products will set you apart

• Able to read API docs and work through integration details with engineers, including GPS and SIM-based tracking, container tracking feeds, webhooks, and ERP connections

• A data-driven mindset: you can estimate the size of a problem, pick the metric that matters, and build a persuasive case from numbers

• Strong written communication and the ability to align engineering and business teams around a spec


How You Use AI

We give real weight to this. RoaDo PMs are expected to use AI as part of their everyday toolkit.

• You regularly use tools like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor to analyse data and find patterns in product logs, customer tickets, and call notes

• You can quickly build a working prototype or demo to test an idea before engineering time is spent

• You use AI to speed up research, produce first drafts of specs, and challenge your own assumptions early

• You think about how AI can change what our product does for customers, such as reading trade documents automatically or predicting delays, and not only how it speeds up building


Bonus Points

• Background in multi-tenant enterprise SaaS

• Hands-on experience with freight forwarding, 3PL, or shipping line software, or with platforms like ICEGATE, PCS, or ULIP

• Exposure to multimodal freight across road, rail, sea, and air

• Working knowledge of Mixpanel, Metabase, Jira, or similar tools

About

While we’re rooting for them, we’re building what comes after. We're based in New York and backed by Y Combinator, General Catalyst, 186 Ventures, Reach Capital and many more. We raised an oversubscribed seed round from some of the best investors in Silicon Valley. Our team includes AI product leaders from companies like Google, physician executives from major health systems, and more.


About the Role

We're looking for a Product Manager, AI to join our team in our Bangalore office. With how AI models are evolving, we don't believe in traditional roles. Whereas in an old-school company you may write long PRDs and hand off to designers and engineering, and spend weeks in back and forths trying to get 1 feature approved, we operate completely differently. Here's what your day-to-day may look like:

  • Instead of writing PRD's, you'll build prototypes.
  • You'll be responsible for prioritizing which pain points to solve, outlining how we should solve them, and designing the user experience yourself as well (with the power of our AI design tools).
  • At any given time, you may be using AI coding tools and AI design tools to parallel track prototypes for 5-10 large features.
  • Rather than waiting weeks for approvals, features you prototype will be handed off to engineering and be shipped into production an average of 2-5 days.
  • You will talk to customers and research the domain deeply - becoming an expert for the team on domain knowledge and product strategy.


Requirements

  • Prior experience working as a Product Manager at a venture backed startup.
  • Either (A) strong experience professionally as a software engineer, or (B) exceptional UX design skills. Must be multifaceted in one of these 2 ways.

Associate Product Manager

at GeoIQ

Posted by Jancy Challam

Bengaluru (Bangalore) · 1 - 3 years · Raised funding · Posted 3 Nov 2026

Product Management
Product owner

Position Overview:

We are building a new retail merchandising platform on top of that data. It answers what to stock, how much, and in which store, combining sales, catalogue, and customer data with GeoIQ’s location attributes at retail scale: thousands of stores, tens of thousands of SKUs, decisions made weekly.


As the product manager on this platform, you will own how those decisions reach the people who make them: category managers, planners and store operations teams. The models are being built alongside the product, so you will decide what gets built, in what order, and how its output fits into a buyer’s weekly planning cycle. You will work every day with data science and engineering, and what you ship changes what a store actually orders.


Responsibilities:

  • Own one or more platform modules (demand forecasting, assortment planning, replenishment, new-launch allocation) from problem definition through to adoption.
  • Spend time with merchandisers, category managers and store teams to understand how buying and replenishment decisions are made today, often in spreadsheets, and where that process breaks.
  • Write specs that data science and engineering can build from: the decision being supported, its inputs, the business rules and constraints (minimum display quantities, pack sizes, warehouse reserves, brand rules), and what a good output looks like.
  • Design the workflows that let planners act on model output with confidence: recommendation screens, overrides, explanations and exception queues.
  • Define success metrics with the business (sell-through, stockouts, inventory turns, forecast accuracy, recommendation acceptance) and set up pilot-versus-control rollouts to measure them.
  • Run pilots with store clusters and categories, gather feedback, and decide what changes before a module scales to the full network.
  • Lead discovery when the platform extends to new brands and markets, each with its own data, supply chain and planning process.
  • Keep the roadmap, priorities and trade-offs clear to merchandising, category, supply chain and leadership teams.


Expectations:

  • Work experience: 2–5 years, with at least 2 years in product management
  • Prior experience taking a product from problem definition to adoption by real users
  • Comfortable with data: able to write SQL, work through a spreadsheet model, and read a model evaluation or A/B test result
  • Clear written communication, including specs that engineers and data scientists can build from without a meeting
  • Understanding of how ML-driven products differ: probabilistic outputs, accuracy limits, and the need for user overrides
  • Experience with B2B, internal tools or data-heavy products will be an added advantage
  • Experience in retail, e-commerce, merchandising, supply chain or inventory planning will be an added advantage
  • Prior experience as an analyst, engineer or data scientist will be an added advantage


Join us early and own the product that decides what thousands of stores stock each week, working directly with the merchants who use it and the team that builds it.

Roles and Responsibilities for Product Owner / Data Solution Specialist


Role purpose


Own and drive the business and data requirements for assigned workstreams, translating business needs into clear, actionable requirements for architecture, modelling, engineering and reporting teams, while coordinating the relevant business and technology SMEs through design, validation and sign-off.


Key responsibilities

• Drive requirements and scope definition for the assigned data product/workstream and maintain clear traceability through design and delivery.

• Identify and coordinate regional and in-market business owners/working teams required to validate requirements and make decisions.

• Translate business requirements into data requirements, including critical data elements, KPIs, dimensions, source-data needs and derived-field/business logic.

• Work closely with Market IT, Business Data Architects, Data Modellers and Data Engineers to understand source systems and support mapping of source attributes into the target data model. The PO is expected to orchestrate this activity, not replace the relevant technical SMEs.

• Facilitate validation of mapped and unmapped data requirements, default values, consolidation/business rules and target-model requirements with business stakeholders.

• Provide business inputs into data-model, data-mart and reporting/dashboard design, including wireframes where relevant.

• Drive stakeholder reviews, requirement/design decisions and formal business sign-offs. 

• Support delivery iteratively. Where requirements are substantially understood, progress agreed tranches rather than waiting for every outstanding item before engineering begins.

• Work alongside the Project Manager on dependencies, decisions and stakeholder mobilisation; project capacity management and overall programme coordination remain PM responsibilities.


Experience/profile required

• 7+ yrs of strong hands-on Product Owner, Business Analyst or Data Solution Specialist experience in enterprise data programmes.

• Demonstrable data-mart / data-warehouse delivery experience and ability to work across source-to-target mapping, business rules, data models and reporting requirements.

• Strong commercial insurance data knowledge is highly desirable, particularly policy, product, underwriting and financial dimensions. Reinsurance experience would be advantageous for relevant workstreams.

• Comfortable working across business, Market IT, architecture, data modelling, engineering and BI teams.

• Able to challenge requirements, structure ambiguity, drive decisions and obtain stakeholder sign-off rather than acting solely as a requirements coordinator.

• Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills across regional and market teams.

• Strong problem-solving abilities with an emphasis on data-driven decision-making

About the Role

Antier Solutions is looking for a technically strong AI Solution Architect to drive the architecture, design, and technical execution of AI-powered solutions.


The role requires a combination of deep technical expertise, architectural ownership, and the ability to guide engineering teams in building scalable, production-ready AI systems. The individual will evaluate business problems, define technical approaches, make architecture decisions, and work closely with developers and stakeholders to translate ideas into working solutions.


This is a hands-on architecture and technical leadership role, not one limited to documentation, project coordination, or pre-sales presentations.


Key Responsibilities


1. AI Architecture & Solution Design

  • Design end-to-end architectures for AI, Generative AI, LLM-based applications, and agentic AI systems.
  • Evaluate and select appropriate models, frameworks, orchestration approaches, and technology stacks.
  • Design solutions involving RAG, AI agents, workflow automation, APIs, databases, and enterprise integrations.
  • Define architecture standards covering scalability, security, performance, maintainability, and deployment.
  • Evaluate technical feasibility, identify risks, and recommend practical implementation approaches.


2. Technical Leadership & Implementation

  • Provide architectural direction and technical guidance to AI engineers and developers.
  • Review proposed designs and implementation approaches, identifying technical gaps and potential bottlenecks.
  • Establish reusable architecture patterns, development standards, and engineering best practices.
  • Troubleshoot complex technical challenges and contribute hands-on where necessary.
  • Guide teams in adopting AI-assisted development and agentic workflows where they improve engineering productivity.


3. Production Readiness & Quality

  • Design solutions with appropriate authentication, access controls, logging, monitoring, testing, and evaluation mechanisms.
  • Address AI-specific challenges such as hallucinations, retrieval quality, model selection, latency, reliability, and inference costs.
  • Define appropriate human oversight and validation mechanisms for sensitive or consequential workflows.
  • Guide deployment decisions across suitable cloud, on-premise, and hybrid environments.


4. Business Alignment & Delivery Ownership

  • Understand business requirements and translate them into implementable technical solutions.
  • Work with stakeholders to establish scope, dependencies, estimates, resource requirements, and delivery milestones.
  • Collaborate with engineering and delivery teams to move solutions from proof of concept to production.
  • Balance rapid execution with architectural quality, maintainability, and commercial feasibility.
  • Communicate technical decisions, risks, and trade-offs clearly to business and technical stakeholders.


Required Skills & Experience

  • B.Tech, BE, MCA, MSc, or equivalent technical qualification in Computer Science, IT, Data Science, or a related discipline.
  • 8+ years of overall experience in software engineering, AI engineering, solution architecture, or related technical roles.
  • Strong hands-on experience building AI/ML or Generative AI applications, with demonstrated responsibility for architecture and implementation decisions.
  • Strong understanding of LLMs, RAG pipelines, agentic AI systems, tool calling, orchestration, and AI-driven automation.
  • Experience with Python and relevant AI frameworks, libraries, and integration technologies.
  • Strong understanding of APIs, databases, data pipelines, distributed systems, and application architecture.
  • Experience evaluating AI solutions for accuracy, reliability, performance, security, and cost.
  • Ability to guide developers, review technical approaches, resolve complex problems, and establish reusable engineering practices.
  • Experience deploying or supporting AI applications in production environments.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and technical decision-making skills.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience architecting multi-agent systems or complex AI automation workflows.
  • Exposure to cloud platforms, containerization, CI/CD, observability, and scalable AI infrastructure.
  • Experience mentoring engineering teams and introducing new AI development practices.
  • Experience with enterprise AI deployments, international clients, or technically complex business environments.


﻿Ideal Candidate Profile

  • We are looking for an individual who can independently own technical architecture, guide engineering teams, and make sound implementation decisions. The candidate should combine hands-on AI expertise with the ability to turn business requirements into scalable, production-ready solutions.
  • Candidates whose experience is limited to AI research, business analysis, project coordination, or pre-sales documentation without meaningful technical implementation and architecture ownership may not be suitable.

### Customers & Market

- Speak directly with customers and prospects.

- Understand how they currently solve problems and where existing tools fail.

- Run product demos and gather structured feedback.

- Separate individual customer requests from broader product opportunities.

- Use customer conversations to continuously refine product strategy.


### Launch & Growth - Own launch strategy for the products and features you build.

- Define positioning, messaging, demos, onboarding, and initial adoption strategy.

- Work across product, engineering, sales, and customers to make launches successful.

- Measure what happened after launch and iterate quickly.


## What We're Looking For

-You likely have **2–4 years of experience** across product, engineering, startups, consulting, AI, or related roles. More importantly, you should have: - **~1 year of hands-on experience building with LLMs, agents, or AI applications.**

- Built actual AI workflows rather than only used ChatGPT or managed an AI project.

- Strong product judgment and ability to simplify complicated problems. - Comfort working with engineers and understanding technical trade-offs.

- Ability to perform deep market and customer research independently. - Strong written and verbal communication.

- High ownership — you naturally move from identifying a problem to getting something shipped.

- Comfort operating in an environment where the answer is often not known beforehand.


## Two Traits We Care About Deeply

### Constraint Thinking Great product people don't start with: *"What could we build?"* They start with: *"Given our users, technology, time, team, data, and constraints, what is the smartest thing we can build?"*


We value people who can reduce a large possibility space into a small number of high-leverage decisions. You should be able to distinguish between: -

interesting vs. useful,

- possible vs. reliable, AI Product Manager 2 / 4 AI Product Manager - demoable vs. production-ready,

- customer requests vs. underlying problems,

- AI capability vs. AI product.


### Grounded Energy AI moves incredibly fast, and it is easy to either become overly skeptical or overly excited. We want someone who has **high energy without hype**. You should be excited enough to constantly experiment with new technology, while grounded enough to recognize its limitations. You should naturally ask:

- Does this actually work?

- How often does it fail?

- What happens at scale?

- Can we evaluate it?

- Will customers actually change their behaviour for this?

- Is AI even necessary here?


## You Might Be a Great Fit If You have independently done things like: - Built an agent over a weekend to test a product idea.

- Compared multiple LLMs for a real use case.

- Created an eval dataset to test AI quality.

- Used tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP, Langfuse, or similar systems.

- Automated parts of your own product or research workflow with agents.

- Interviewed users and changed the product based on what you learned.

- Gone from idea to prototype to customer feedback to production. - Read product documentation, GitHub repos, Reddit discussions, research papers, and competitor products to understand a market deeply.

## This Role Is Probably Not For You If

- You primarily see PM as backlog management and sprint coordination. - You need detailed requirements before you can start working.

- You prefer delegating prototyping and experimentation entirely to engineering.

- You haven't spent meaningful time building with modern AI tools.

- You enjoy creating large strategy documents more than testing ideas with users.

- You are uncomfortable making decisions with incomplete information.


## What Success Looks Like Within your first few months, you should be able to independently: AI Product Manager 3 / 4 AI Product Manager - understand a customer problem,

- research the market,

- identify a promising product opportunity,

- prototype an AI workflow,

- define how its quality should be evaluated,

- work with engineering to productionize it,

- speak with early users,

- launch it,

- measure adoption,

- and recommend what we should do next.

Product Manager – AI/GenAI

Our AI platform that lets people ask questions of their enterprise data in natural language and get trustworthy answers. The hard part isn't the model — it's the fit between what the product can genuinely do and what customers actually need, over data that is never as clean as anyone hopes. We're hiring a Product Manager to own that fit: to do the detailed thinking on customer pain, competitive landscape, and where the technology is going, and to turn it into a sharp, defensible product proposition and roadmap. You'll work closely with the CTO (who currently carries this thinking) and become the person who owns the depth beneath it.


What you'll own

• Proposition & positioning. Take fuzzy capability and turn it into a clear, honest, defensible articulation of what Jiva is, who it's for, and why it wins. Kill the gap between what's sold and what's deliverable.

• Customer intelligence (within the current structure). Sales and Delivery own the customer relationship today; you build the customer picture through them —mining PoC post-mortems, win/loss, readiness audits, sales-call notes, and Delivery's ground truth. Extract real jobs-to-be-done, separate stated wants from underlying pain, and bring a synthesized customer voice into the room. Over time, earn a path to direct customer contact — but you'll start by getting more 

out of the signal the field teams already carry than anyone does today.

• Competitive & technology intelligence. Track the space — RAG, text-to-SQL, tabular/relational foundation models, agentic systems, the commercial players — and synthesize it into product direction. Know what's real and what's marketing.

• Requirements & roadmap. Translate the above into crisp requirements and a prioritized roadmap, in partnership with Engineering. Make the trade-offs explicit.

• Sales & Delivery enablement. Own the "what we can honestly promise" story so field teams stop overselling and start qualifying. You are the source of truth on capability boundaries.


Must-haves

• 5+ years in B2B / enterprise product management, ideally on data, analytics, AI/ML, or platform products.

• Demonstrated ability to frame a proposition — you can show us a product or feature where you turned raw capability into a positioning that won customers. Portfolio evidence, not a claim.

• Technical fluency in AI/data. You understand RAG, LLMs, text-to-SQL, and data quality well enough to judge feasibility vs. hype and to earn engineers' respect. You don't need to code; you need to reason.

• Customer discovery skill — and the resourcefulness to apply it 

indirectly. You've run structured discovery and can distinguish what customers say from what they need. Just as important here: you can extract sharp customer insight secondhand — through sales and delivery teams, deal histories, 

and product usage — because you won't have direct customer access on day one.

• Evidence-driven and structured. You validate before you evangelize. Strong written thinker — you can put a proposition on one page and defend it.


Nice-to-have

• Exposure to NL→SQL, semantic layers, knowledge graphs, or enterprise data governance.

• 0-to-1 or turnaround experience — comfort building the function, not just running it.

• Experience selling into or building for regulated / data-sensitive enterprises

What You'll Own?

• Spend time with customers and internal teams to understand workflows, constraints, and the real problem behind requests.

• Translate ambiguous operational problems into clear product requirements, user journeys, and measurable outcomes.

• Work closely with engineering and design from discovery through rollout rather than handing off specifications.

• Prioritize based on customer impact, product strategy, effort, risk, and reuse across customers.

• Define success metrics and evaluate whether shipped products actually improve the workflow.

• Own launches, feedback loops, adoption, and iteration after release.

• Identify patterns across customer requests and turn them into reusable platform capabilities instead of one-off customizations.

• Maintain clarity on what we are building, why we are building it, and what we deliberately are not building.


What We're Looking For?

• 1-5 years of product, engineering, analytics, consulting, operations, or adjacent experience; level will be calibrated to experience.

• Strong problem decomposition and structured thinking.

• Ability to understand technical systems, APIs, data flows, and constraints well enough to work deeply with engineers.

• Excellent written and verbal communication.

• Comfort speaking with customers and asking detailed questions until the underlying workflow is understood.

• Bias toward evidence, prototypes, and shipped outcomes rather than process for its own sake.

• Ability to operate with ambiguity and make sensible trade-offs.


Nice to Have

• Experience with B2B SaaS, enterprise software, workflow products, fintech, or AI-assisted products.

• Technical background or prior engineering experience.

• Experience working with APIs, integrations, analytics, or operational products.

• Experience taking a product from discovery through adoption.


How Product Works Here?

Product managers are expected to understand the problem deeply, not act as ticket routers. The best solution may be a new feature, a platform primitive, a workflow change, an API, or deciding not to build something. Success is measured by customer and product outcomes, not PRD volume.

Job Description

This is a remote position.


Experience Level

We're looking for a seasoned Product Owner with at least 2–4 years of experience owning a product backlog end-to-end within an Agile delivery environment. You should be a "delivery craftsperson" who can demonstrate a track record of turning ambiguous, cross-team requirements into shipped, working software — with particular comfort operating inside platforms where your product's success depends on coordination with teams you don't manage.

 

Role Overview

As a Product Owner, you will own the backlog and delivery cadence for one product within a tightly interconnected platform, where your product's roadmap depends on — and feeds into — several sibling products. You'll act as the point of alignment between engineering teams, supporting product managers, and client stakeholders, translating business and compliance needs into backlog items ready for a development team to execute against.

A key part of the role is holding the line on requirements quality: defining clear acceptance criteria before work enters a sprint, and sequencing competing demands — new features, maintenance of live services, and production support — that your team carries simultaneously. Because your product does not operate in isolation, a large part of the job is coordinating dependencies across teams that don't report to you.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Backlog Ownership & Requirements Definition: Own and prioritize the product backlog; define acceptance criteria for accuracy, completeness, and readiness before stories are marked sprint-ready.
  • Cross-Team Dependency Coordination: Sequence and negotiate delivery across multiple dependent engineering teams (platform, integration, infrastructure, and adjacent product teams), since most features require multi-team scheduling rather than single-team execution.
  • Delivery Prioritization Under Competing Demands: Balance new feature development, maintenance of live production services, and active production support within the same backlog, without letting one silently starve the others.
  • Domain Ramp-Up: Build working depth in the specific technical and regulatory domain tied to your assigned product — this may include healthcare EDI transaction standards, web-automation/data-extraction reliability, credential and access-security models, or regulated payments and remittance processing, depending on placement.
  • Stakeholder & Requirements Governance: Partner with the supporting Product Manager and client-side stakeholders to close open requirement decisions before development starts, hold sign-off discipline, and manage rework risk from late-stage scope changes.
  • Data & Interface Quality Ownership: Where your product's output feeds downstream systems, own the interface contract (field definitions, data completeness, naming) to prevent avoidable rework further down the chain.


Requirements

What We're Looking For

  • Proven Product Ownership Experience: Track record owning a backlog end-to-end in an Agile environment, ideally within a platform where products are tightly coupled rather than independent.
  • Domain Adaptability: Comfort ramping quickly into unfamiliar technical or regulatory domains — some assignments require near-immediate fluency (e.g., regulated payments, EDI standards), while others allow for a longer runway.
  • Cross-Functional Coordination Skills: Demonstrated ability to sequence work and resolve competing priorities across multiple engineering teams that don't report into the same chain.
  • Analytical Rigor: Ability to write precise, testable acceptance criteria and reason through data quality or completeness gaps before they become delivery blockers.
  • Strong Stakeholder Communication: Comfortable representing product status and trade-offs to both engineering teams and client-facing stakeholders, in plain, non-technical language when needed.
  •  Judgment Under Ambiguity: Able to recognize when a decision needs escalation versus independent ownership — particularly important for the more regulation-heavy assignments, where working without senior support isn't advisable early on.


Benefits

Life at Incubyte 

We are a remote-first company with structured flexibility. Teams commit to shared rhythms during core hours, ensuring smooth collaboration while maintaining autonomy. Twice a year, we come together in person for a co-working sprint and once a year for a retreat - with all travel expenses covered. 

Our environment is built for crafters: pairing, refactoring, experimenting with AI, and pushing the boundaries of software excellence. We are all lifelong learners, and our work is our passion. 


Perks

  • Dedicated learning & development budget. 
  • Sponsorship for conference talks. 
  • Comprehensive medical & term insurance. 
  • Employee-friendly leave policies. 
  • Home Office fund 
  • Medical Insurance
